To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(i) anti-TrkA IgG is an effective agonist for TrkA, and (ii) anti-Trk IgG and Fab block NGF binding to TrkA.

the binding of NGF and anti-TrkA IgG to the TrkA receptor induces the same biological effects on PC12 cells, suggesting that the binding of ligands to receptors may not always be necessary to induce receptor signaling.
the extracellular region of TrkA can be expressed in insect cells and that anti-TrkA antibodies can be used to study the NGF response.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel approach for the study of the NGF signaling pathway.
the development of antibodies that recognize the extracellular domain of the trkA receptor.
the use of polyclonal antibodies to study the NGF response pathway.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the biological effects of trkA are mediated through cross-linking, and that the biological effects are not due to a direct effect of NGF binding to the receptor.

trkA is the only high-affinity NGF-binding protein on PC12 cells, that the low-affinity binding sites on PC 12 cells are all LNGFRs, and that NGF induces its effects on PC12 cells through trkA cross-linkage.
trkA is the sole receptor for high-affinity NGF, and the LNGFR is the receptor for low-affinity NGFR binding.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
NGF induces trkA receptor dimerization or oligomerization, and this event is sufficient to produce a biological response in the target cell.
the anti-trkA antibodies are specific and effective for NGF binding and receptor activation.
the NGF receptor is composed of two components, trkA and LNGFR, and the NGF binding site is composed of two binding sites on each component.
The main takeaway from our work is that
trkA is a high-affinity receptor that is essential for NGF signaling.
the NGF response pathway in PC12 cells and in neurons is initiated by receptor cross-linking, and not by NGF-induced dimerization.
cross-linking trkA with anti-trkA IgG mimics many of the cellular effects of NGFs.
